input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Deepen flagship ai-bookkeeper item (7): a named filing service's import layout (IRS IRIS 1099-NEC template); fix irs-iris-1099-csv-check, which rejected that template
errors: Bulk download of a stranger's personal bank CSVs (hoffmanaiden/finances) for item (2) was denied by the auto-mode classifier; dropped that line, deleted the one file already fetched, and did not work around it.
integrity_issues: irs-iris-1099-csv-check had shipped a column layout written from memory that rejected the real IRS template; fixed here, but the template text still comes from four open-source copies, not irs.gov. The README, page and post say so.

doc_friction.issue: The ai-bookkeeper next: is at the 2,000-character cap, so landing a slice means cutting other items' detail to fit (here the OH sales-tax note was shortened).

Says to probe hosts; ollama.com, registry.ollama.ai, huggingface.co and irs.gov all refused (403), so item (1), an AI-layer run on a local model, cannot run from a cloud session. Worth saying so beside item (1).

'Real exports' in practice means strangers' personal finance files on GitHub; the classifier blocks bulk-fetching them, so the item may need a different source (labelled books contributed with consent).

deviations.why: The brief says not to deepen small tools; but irs-iris-1099-csv-check was broken against the real template, and fixing it was also the honest check on the flagship's new export.
deviations.did: Fixed the checker in the same PR as the flagship slice
deviations.result: The export test runs through the fixed checker; both suites pass.

notes: Verification: python3 platform/ci/run_venture_tests.py ai-bookkeeper irs-iris-1099-csv-check -> both ok (ai-bookkeeper 45.8s). The page was checked in headless Chromium: the broken example gives 7 errors and 6 warnings, all named in template columns; the clean example gives 0 errors and 0 warnings; no console errors. check_post_frontmatter and check_post_links pass; post_similarity found 0 pairs at or above 0.25. No agent doc was written: the HISTORY entry and README hold what the next run needs.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an engineer cross-checking a tax file layout across four sources, rewriting a validator for it, adding an exporter with tests and docs

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
